title: The profile history chart's tests check an old bar chart the screen no longer draws
what: The profile history chart is now a line chart with its own placing and picking rules. The old bar-chart rules (where each bar sits, what a tap does, which bar shows first, the side scale and the bottom labels) are still in the app and still tested, but the screen never uses them. One even disagrees with the screen: the old rule shows the newest bar first, the screen shows the whole range's total. The tests pass while saying nothing about what the member sees.
expected: Tests check the rules the chart really uses; retired chart rules are removed.
fix_line: Delete the unused bar-chart rules and their tests, and test the line chart's own picking instead

title: The retired 'swap an exercise' part of the Balance check is still in the app and still tested
what: On 13 Nov the owner moved swap advice to the Up next tip only, and the Balance check card stopped offering a swap. The code that picked the exercise to take out, the 'best for this muscle' list, and their words are still kept and still tested, but nothing in the app calls them. The feature list still says the card offers one exercise.
expected: Retired swap code and its tests are removed; the feature description matches the card.
fix_line: Remove the unused swap picking and its tests, and update the feature description

title: The weigh-in list's 'page at a time' rule is used only by its own test
what: A fix once made the weigh-in history load 60 rows at a time with 'Show older'. The Measures page that replaced it lists every entry at once, so this paging rule is no longer used anywhere in the app. Only a test keeps it alive, so it looks like a working feature when it is not.
expected: Unused rules are deleted with their tests.
fix_line: Delete the unused paging rule and its test

title: A damaged saved focus block or set plan is thrown away without a trace
what: If the saved Balance check state or a routine exercise's set-by-set plan (warm-up, drop, failure sets) cannot be read, the app quietly treats it as empty: the focus block disappears, or the exercise falls back to plain sets. Nothing is logged, so if a member says their warm-up sets vanished there is no record of why.
expected: The fallback stays, but each one writes a log line saying what could not be read.
fix_line: Log a short error line in both fallbacks before returning the empty value

title: The same small sums are written out again in several places
what: Days between two dates is worked out by hand in six places although the app has one shared rule for it; a middle value (median) is written four times, one of them rounding and the others not; and 'longest run of weeks in a row' is written twice, once for badges and once for the year review. They agree today, but a later fix to one copy will not reach the others.
expected: One shared rule per sum, used everywhere.
fix_line: Use the shared date and streak rules and one median helper

title: A Target-line test fails if the build machine is slow, not if the app is wrong
what: One test of the weight ladder times 500 workouts of history with the real clock and fails if it takes over 2 seconds. On a busy cloud build machine this can fail at random and block a release with no real fault.
expected: Speed is checked by counting work or with a far looser bound kept apart from the correctness checks.
fix_line: Move the timing check out of the correctness test or loosen it greatly
